edges.description: Loss of sympathetic vasoconstriction in the lower extremities allows excessive venous pooling upon standing, reducing cardiac preload.
Reduced stroke volume from venous pooling triggers baroreceptor-mediated sympathetic activation and compensatory heart rate increase.
Reduced venous return lowers stroke volume and cerebral perfusion on standing, which patients experience as lightheadedness.
When the compensatory heart-rate response fails to maintain cerebral perfusion, the fall in cerebral blood flow can progress to transient loss of consciousness.
Sustained reduction in cerebral perfusion during upright posture impairs attention, concentration, and working memory.
Altered cerebral perfusion during orthostatic stress contributes to the headache reported on standing.
Blood pooling in the dependent extremities on standing produces the bluish-red discoloration and sluggish peripheral circulation.
The exaggerated upright heart rate is perceived directly by the patient as a rapid or forceful heartbeat.
Sustained tachycardia raises myocardial oxygen demand and shortens diastolic filling time, which can present as exertional or orthostatic chest discomfort.
Tachycardia with a reduced stroke volume limits the cardiac output available on standing and exertion, producing breathlessness.
Because the heart rate reserve is already consumed at rest in the upright posture, little remains for exertion, capping achievable workload.
The chronic effort of sustaining cardiac output through heart rate alone, together with reduced stroke volume, leaves patients persistently exhausted.
Excessive catecholamine release drives the exaggerated heart rate response.
Elevated circulating norepinephrine acts on peripheral beta-2 adrenergic receptors in skeletal muscle to produce the postural tremor seen in hyperadrenergic POTS.
Autoimmune-mediated damage to autonomic nerves may cause the partial sympathetic denervation seen in neuropathic POTS.
AT1R autoantibody activity may disrupt angiotensin II receptor responsiveness and contribute indirectly to low effective circulating volume or low preload in a subset of POTS.
Autonomic dysregulation extends beyond the cardiovascular system to gastrointestinal motility, so the same disturbance produces nausea alongside the orthostatic features.
Viral infection may trigger autoantibody production against autonomic receptors.
Cardiac atrophy reduces stroke volume, compounding the effect of venous pooling.

The heart-rate increment measured during standing or head-up tilt is the bedside measurement of the compensatory reflex tachycardia mechanism; the 30 bpm threshold is the diagnostic cut-point applied to that measurement.
Autonomic function testing demonstrating impaired cardiovascular reflexes reports the partial peripheral sympathetic denervation postulated in neuropathic POTS.

The same autonomic testing abnormality also reports the opposite pole of the syndrome, excessive central sympathetic outflow, so the finding is shared across mechanistic subtypes rather than specific to one.

nodes.description: Dysregulation of the autonomic nervous system is the hallmark of POTS, manifesting as impaired cardiovascular reflexes and multi-system autonomic dysfunction.

evidence.reference_title: Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome: clinical presentation, aetiology and management.
evidence.snippet: The aetiology of POTS is largely unknown and three main hypotheses include an autoimmune disorder, abnormally increased sympathetic activity and catecholamine excess, and sympathetic denervation leading to central hypovolaemia and reflex tachycardia.

reports_on.interpretation: Autonomic function testing demonstrating impaired cardiovascular reflexes reports the partial peripheral sympathetic denervation postulated in neuropathic POTS.

The same autonomic testing abnormality also reports the opposite pole of the syndrome, excessive central sympathetic outflow, so the finding is shared across mechanistic subtypes rather than specific to one.

nodes.description: Bluish-red discoloration of the dependent extremities upon standing, reflecting venous pooling and poor peripheral circulation.

Autoantibodies targeting G-protein coupled autonomic receptors may interfere with normal autonomic signaling, contributing to the autonomic dysregulation seen in POTS. Adrenergic and muscarinic receptor antibodies have been reported in some cohorts, while a recent cohort instead found elevated angiotensin II type 1 receptor antibodies, leaving receptor specificity and causality unresolved.

evidence.reference_title: Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome Is Associated With Elevated G-Protein Coupled Receptor Autoantibodies.
evidence.snippet: We detected a significant number of patients with elevated levels of autoantibodies against the adrenergic alpha 1 receptor (89%) and against the muscarinic acetylcholine M4 receptor (53%).

evidence.reference_title: Angiotensin II Type 1 Receptor Autoantibodies in Postural Tachycardia Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Of 17 subjects with POTS, 12 demonstrated significant AT1R antibody activity in immunoglobulin G purified from their serum. No significant AT1R antibody activity was found in the subjects with vasovagal syncope or healthy subjects.

evidence.reference_title: Autoimmune Antibodies in Orthostatic Intolerance Syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Significantly higher levels of angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) autoantibodies were found in the POTS group compared with controls

evidence.reference_title: Autoimmune Antibodies in Orthostatic Intolerance Syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Autoantibody concentration against ADRA1, ADRB1, ADRB2, and M4R were not significantly different between the groups.

nodes.description: Graded exercise programs, particularly recumbent exercise initially, have been shown to improve cardiovascular conditioning, expand blood volume, and reduce orthostatic tachycardia in POTS patients. After 3 months of training, over 50% of patients no longer met criteria for POTS.

evidence.reference_title: Exercise and non-pharmacological treatment of POTS.
evidence.snippet: physical reconditioning with exercise training and volume expansion via increased salt and fluid intake should be initiated early in the course of treatment for patients with POTS if possible. The use of horizontal exercise (e.g., rowing, swimming, recumbent bike, etc.) at the beginning is a critical strategy, allowing patients to exercise while avoiding the upright posture that elicits their POTS symptoms.

evidence.reference_title: Propranolol decreases tachycardia and improves symptoms in the postural tachycardia syndrome: less is more.
evidence.snippet: Low-dose oral propranolol significantly attenuated tachycardia and improved symptoms in POTS. Higher-dose propranolol did not further improve, and may worsen, symptoms.

evidence.reference_title: Low-dose propranolol and exercise capacity in postural tachycardia syndrome: a randomized study.
evidence.snippet: Low-dose propranolol improved VO2max in patients with POTS (24.5 ± 0.7 placebo vs 27.6 ± 1.0 mL/min/kg propranolol; p = 0.024), but not healthy subjects.

nodes.description: Ivabradine selectively inhibits the funny (If) current in sinoatrial node pacemaker cells, lowering heart rate without reducing blood pressure or myocardial contractility. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial it improved heart rate and quality of life in patients with hyperadrenergic POTS.

evidence.reference_title: Randomized Trial of Ivabradine in Patients With Hyperadrenergic Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Ivabradine is safe and effective in significantly improving heart rate and QOL in patients with hyperadrenergic POTS as the predominant subtype.

nodes.description: Alpha-1 adrenergic agonist that promotes peripheral vasoconstriction, improving venous return and reducing orthostatic symptoms.

nodes.description: Pyridostigmine is an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor that enhances cardiovagal (parasympathetic) tone, attenuating orthostatic tachycardia and symptom burden without raising blood pressure. It offers a parasympathomimetic alternative to sympatholytic strategies.

evidence.reference_title: Acetylcholinesterase inhibition improves tachycardia in postural tachycardia syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Acute acetylcholinesterase inhibition significantly attenuated tachycardia in POTS.
